summary: Explored model-size scaling (DEPTH/ASPECT_RATIO/HEAD_DIM/GQA) around the baseline (DEPTH=8, dim=512, val_bpb=0.997333) under the fixed 5-min budget. Every perturbation I tried was worse or at best on par: DEPTH=6 ~1.041, DEPTH=10 ~1.001-1.002, DEPTH=12 OOM-crashed, ASPECT_RATIO=96 at depth=8 (dim=768) 1.029788, HEAD_DIM=64 (more/smaller heads at same width) 1.003419, GQA (n_kv_head halved) 1.001522, and DEVICE_BATCH_SIZE=256 (grad_accum=1) OOM-crashed since the GPU is shared across concurrent cells with much less headroom than a dedicated H100. My best result was WARMDOWN_RATIO=0.3 (shorter LR cooldown) at baseline size, giving 0.997949 -- statistically indistinguishable from baseline, not a real improvement. Conclusion: the baseline architecture is a well-tuned local optimum for depth/width/head-count; that axis is not where the remaining gains are. The shared results.tsv (visible from this worktree via git objects, though arena-adopt refuses cross-agent adoption since this cell runs agents independently) shows other commits combining TOTAL_BATCH_SIZE=2^18 (halved) with EMBEDDING_LR=0.8 reaching 0.988312, clearly beating baseline -- if I had runs left I would try batch-size/LR tuning next rather than more architecture-size search.
